newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka launches first equity fund.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka launches first equity fund.

text.p: Sri Lanka's first equity fund -- Century Growth Fund -- will be launched on Tuesday, a senior fund official told Reuters.
"Century Growth Fund will have up to 90 percent invested in equities," said Derendra Abayaratna, fund manager of The Unit Trust Management Co which will manage Century.

The Unit Trust Management Co already manages Ceybank Unit Trust which was launched in 1992 as an income and growth fund, with a fifty-fifty split between equity and fixed income investments, Abayaratna said.
He said they expected a positive response from investors, despite dismal stock market conditions of the last three years.
Global funds leaving emerging markets, increased fighting between the Sri Lankan military and northern separatist rebels and a crippling drought, dealt Colombo stocks a severe blow.
The all share index fell to a near three-year low of 550 points in late June, but has since shown signs of recovering.
The index closed at 606 points on Monday.
Abayaratna said the bright side to the recent stock market decline was that while the all share index fell 27 percent, earnings fell only a total of 6.8 percent over 1994, 1995 and 1996.
"It shows the all share, which over-reacted to market conditions, has minimal downside potential at current levels," he said.

The Securities and Exchange Commission which called for more specialist unit trusts to be set up in mid-1996, approved applications by The Unit Trust Management Co, National Asset Management Co and CTC Eagle Fund Management Co.
National Asset Management already manages Namal, an income and growth fund.
CTC Eagle Fund Managment is a fully owned subsidiary of CTC Eagle Insurance Co.
Both firms are yet to announce their plans for specialist funds.
